chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:
The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'Excellent is the aid toward taqwa of God — wealth.'

key_terms.الْعَوْنُ: Aid, assistance, support; that which helps one achieve a goal
key_terms.الْغِنَى: Wealth, prosperity, sufficiency, self-reliance; financial abundance that frees one from dependence on others
key_terms.تَقْوَى اللَّهِ: Taqwa of God — God-consciousness, piety, fear of God; the foundational Islamic virtue of awareness of God in all actions
key_terms.نِعْمَ: An Arabic superlative particle of praise meaning 'excellent is' or 'the best'; used to commend something highly

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about wealth and taqwa in Islam?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) affirmed that worldly prosperity and financial sufficiency are among the best aids toward attaining taqwa (God-consciousness). This teaching, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq and the chain of Imams back to the Prophet, appears in al-Kafi's section on utilizing worldly resources for the Hereafter. The early Muslim community would have understood this as endorsing lawful wealth-seeking as a spiritual support, not an obstacle — countering an extreme asceticism that equated poverty with piety.
